Registered in the same change that lands the file; ratchet applies from landing. 2026-07-31: registered settings-redirects - the users/orgs/pedidos pages moved into the settings tab group and the three old routes became redirects, which NOTHING asserted; a later tidy-up deleting three four-line redirect files would pass every gate in this repo and break every external link silently. Registered in the same change that lands the file; ratchet applies from landing. 2026-08-03 (C2): registered integration-write-gate - the `mutates: true` EXECUTION GATE's human half. The gate itself lives in the api executor (pinned by tests/integrations/action-consent.test.ts + tests/security/integration-write-gate.test.ts); this spec is the place a human actually answers it, driven on the SHIPPED Slack package because it carries exactly the two shapes the gate distinguishes (send_message mutates, list_channels does not). Also pins the Rule-7 half: the mutates:false action gains NO chip, no control and no prompt. Re-runnable by construction (it clears any standing approval first and revokes what it granted); nothing is executed against Slack - approving records an answer, it does not call the integration. Zero console errors + no non-asset 404s. Registered in the same change that lands the file; ratchet applies from landing. 2026-08-03 (CS7): registered citius-sync-outcome - the Citius sync OUTCOME panel on /integrations, i.e. the one surface where a lawyer learns whether their inbox is provably complete. The three states (Completa / INCOMPLETA / Falhou) are asserted DISTINGUISHABLE the way a person perceives them: the spec reads COMPUTED styles off the live page (accent-bar width, border and surface colour, chip fill, headline size/weight) and requires INCOMPLETA to carry weight Completa does not and a colour family Falhou does not - a class-name rename cannot satisfy it. Plus the copy each state must carry (INCOMPLETA says notifications may be missing AND that the read pointer did not advance and the next run re-sweeps from the same point; Falhou says the sync never ran and never prints a per-run '0 notificações', which would read as 'there were none'), and a fourth test pinning that a 404 (CS6's flag defaulting OFF) renders NO panel at all. Registered in the same change that lands the file; ratchet applies from landing. 2026-08-03 (D3): registered integration-achieve - `achieve` (EXECUTE-OR-AUTHOR) end to end. The browser is the HUMAN (real UI login, a real gateway key minted on the real /settings/api-keys page, the real write-gate dialog on the integrations page) and an ordinary HTTP client carrying that key is the AGENT, so the property that matters is asserted across a real socket: the agent's goal is refused at C2's write gate with the typed consentRequest, the SAME key is refused 401 at BOTH self-approval doors (POST .../approval and D3's POST .../trust), the human approves on the real page, and only then does the identical call get past the gate - answering not_connected, i.e. Slack is never contacted. HERMETIC AND LLM-FREE by construction rather than by stubbing: every assertion sits on a path that refuses BEFORE any model call or outbound request - the gate answers before a credential is loaded, authoring on a SHIPPED package answers baseline_package before drafting, and the promotion route is refused at admission. The author arm's happy path is deterministic in api/tests/contract/integrations-achieve.test.ts, where only the model turn is faked at the seam. Re-runnable: it revokes the approval it grants and the key it mints. 2026-08-08 (WS8a): registered knowledge-shared-scope - the Biblioteca's `_shared` legal-corpus visibility fix (the operator's "the knowledge base is empty" report: the 262k+-document reserved corpus was always SEARCHABLE, never BROWSABLE - a fresh org's own vault is genuinely empty, which is what made it look empty). So the three requests addressing `_shared` (collections?scope=shared, documents?scope=shared, search) are intercepted with fixtures validated in-spec against the shared CollectionsResponse/DocumentsResponse/KnowledgeSearchResponse schemas; every scope=org request, the login and the rest of the dashboard are live and unstubbed - a route handler branches on the `scope` query param and calls `route.continue()` for anything not addressed to `_shared`, so a regression in the real org-vault path fails this spec exactly as a stub-only spec could not catch. Three tests: a dropped file stages as a visible chip; a long paste (>800 chars) stages as a text attachment and never fills the textarea; a short paste is left untouched (no preventDefault on the composer's paste handler), proving the hook does not interfere with normal typing/pasting. The in-session composer (chat-panel.tsx) shares the identical drop/paste handler logic and is covered at the unit level instead (components/chat-panel-composer) since reaching it here needs a session with content first. The runtime is now frame-aware and this spec pins the handshake, LLM-free and stub-free: (1) a page on the dashboard origin frames the featured Nucleo, a REAL click calls signIn() (production fidelity: activation gates popups there; the harness itself runs Chromium with --disable-popup-blocking, so the popup-BLOCKED branch - frame left alone + console warning - is pinned by the served-app contract strings, not here), and the assertions are that a NEW top-level window opens on the SSO leg (unconfigured e2e answers the start URL 503 - same URL, still top-level; an SSO-configured stack 302s straight to the provider, so every navigation assertion accepts start-URL-or-provider-authority) while the frame provably never leaves the app document; (2) the same click on the TOP-LEVEL app still navigates in place (the byte-compat path, unchanged). The injected-runtime strings are separately pinned in the served-app contract suite; the popup half (named '__ekoa_sso_' window reloads its framed opener and closes itself after the callback lands back on /apps/<id>/) was probe-verified at registration but is deliberately NOT a committed assertion (window.close timing is browser-dependent; the frame-side session poll (the quiet /api/app-sso/session probe against a popup-open baseline, reload only on session CHANGE; definition AND invocation string-pinned in the served-app contract suite) is the fallback that makes the committed half sufficient). Verified green at registration against a scratch --built stack, and verified to FAIL against the pre-change runtime (the framed test times out waiting for a popup that never opens) - the spec discriminates. Registered in the same change that lands the file; ratchet applies from landing. 2026-08-15 (same-day second pass): app-sso-frame gained a THIRD test - cancelling the popup must SETTLE the flow (the frame reloads), pinning a regression the first version of the fix introduced and that was measured on the real customer ERP: with the frame no longer navigating away, the app's own sign-in button stayed disabled with its spinner running forever because nothing told it the flow had ended. Verified green against the fixed runtime and RED against the old one (that run fails both framed tests), so the new test is not vacuous. 2026-08-17: registered schedules - the timer rail's UI driven end to end against the REAL api (no stubs): sidebar nav -> /schedules; create a MANUAL-task schedule through the real form (target card, recurrence builder, the SERVER-computed preview via POST /api/v1/schedules/preview); the row lists under the when-grouping with its humanised cadence; run-now (202) surfaces the pending run in the TASK INBOX; complete removes it; delete leaves the estate as found (re-runnable). Separately the module docblock described 'the owner's PERSISTENT context' with concurrent runs sharing cookies while the composition root has always returned browser.newContext(); reading the docblock instead of the composition root produced wrong audit conclusions twice, so the ACTUAL model (fresh per session, no jar shared across runs or owners) is now pinned by test rather than asserted by comment. Each property asserted separately: the value is typed as out-of-band CDP key events and locator.fill() is NEVER called (fill sets the DOM value directly, observable to any page script); fill-and-submit are ONE unit so control never returns to the agent with a filled password field on the page, which is what makes read-back impossible by construction; origin is checked BEFORE the unwrap so a wrong-origin page never causes a decrypt; the Cofre lock applies exactly as it does to any other consumer; suppression is a PRECONDITION - the typist REFUSES to fill when it cannot confirm the screencast is stopped, and the decisive assertion there is that NOTHING was typed; the credential window resumes even when the fill throws; and an unknown form (no password field, or one still present after submit) pauses for the relay rather than being handed to the fixer to guess at. The suite pins the properties that matter: a v2 row cannot be decrypted under another TENANT; a fresh data key per record means two encryptions of the same value differ; tampering fails GCM auth; a malformed v2 string is refused rather than guessed at; a wrapper failure SURFACES rather than degrading to a weaker key; and — the adoption property — a legacy v1 row still decrypts unchanged, so this needed no migration flag day. Origins are DERIVED from the cookies rather than guessed by the caller — a caller that guesses either breaks the session or over-binds it — and a capture with no derivable origin is REFUSED at capture time, where the reason is obvious, rather than becoming replayable anywhere. A bridge token is a 600s bearer credential AND attachLiveConnection retires the incumbent on redial (correct for a daemon reconnecting after a blip); compose the two and a captured token did not merely replay, it EVICTED the real daemon and received that pairing's delegate frames. The decisive case is therefore not 'the replay is refused' but 'the replay is refused AND the real daemon still holds its socket' — a fix that rejected after handleUpgrade would pass the first assertion and still have lost the daemon. Tokens now carry a jti spent exactly once; a token with NO jti is refused outright rather than admitted unspendable (the bypass a jti-if-present design would leave); the ?token= query form is gone, pinned by a case proving the SAME token works in the header so the refusal is about transport, not validity; and the token-epoch check reaches the bridge, including the half that connect-time checks cannot give — an ALREADY-OPEN socket is dropped when the epoch bumps, the account deactivates or billing locks, because a WS is authorised once and then lives for hours. Single-use compatibility with the shipped daemon was VERIFIED by reading ../ekoa-bridge (mints fresh before every dial, no caching), not assumed, and all three controls were plant-tested red before landing. And bridge-secret-delivery.test.ts (10) — J-3. secret.deliver is the only frame carrying credential material. The nonce is REDEEMED BEFORE the unwrap, so a replay causes no decrypt and no second copy on the wire; the suite asserts the wire length, not just the rejection, because a design that refused after sending would satisfy a rejects-check and still have leaked. A delivery is bound to the pairing it was authorised for (so a caller that can influence the pairing id cannot redirect a credential to another of the org's machines), an offline machine is a REFUSAL rather than a delivery that never left, and the redeem-first trade-off — a failed send consumes the authorisation, so retry means a NEW invocation — is pinned as a decision on record rather than something a later reader 'fixes' back into a replay window. The daemon-side half (RAM only, absent from config.json and the ledger, zeroized) is a COUNTERPART obligation flagged C6/C7 in docs/bridge-counterpart-changes.md and tested in that repo; this suite does not pretend to prove it. And write-approval.test.ts (18) — J-7, two authorisation bugs sharing one theme: a control that looked like a control. (1) The daemon gates a first write on confirmed===true and its header says the user assents Cortex-side; nothing Cortex-side checked it and agents/sdk-tools.ts literally INSTRUCTED the model to set it, so — because delegateToLocal passes the model's TaskProgram through verbatim and SIGNS it with the pairing secret — Cortex's signature laundered a model self-assertion into an authorisation the daemon trusts. The suite pins the module AND the wiring, and the decisive delegation case asserts NOTHING WAS DISPATCHED rather than merely that the call returned denied: a check that ran after the signature would be no check at all. Approvals are per-file, single-use, non-transferable across users or machines, and expiring, because a confirmation is an answer to a question asked seconds ago. A malformed task is treated as carrying no approval, never as an accidental allow. (2) The command shape wildcarded exactly the dangerous part: `cat ~/notes.txt` stored as `cat <FILE>` matched `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa`, and `curl -s <URL>` turned one approved API call into an approved EXFILTRATION primitive. command-shape.ts had already made this argument once for `bash -c` (a shell body is arbitrary code, never a class); J-7 finishes it — there is no argument class that can be safely wildcarded, so the shape is the exact command, and pre-J-7 wildcard rows are refused rather than left to match. Approvals also gained tenant scoping, machine binding and a 90-day TTL, none of which existed. The second bug is LATENT (local_command is unreachable end-to-end — the composition root leaves setDaemonConnectionResolver on its default), which is exactly when it is cheapest to fix and easiest to forget. Both controls plant-tested red before landing. And bridge-audit.test.ts (8) — J-6. Cortex persisted NOTHING about bridge invocations: only kind==='read' ledger rows left the machine, into a 15-minute in-memory Map built to render a trust chip. The plane with the most physical access to a user's data — the one reading their files and running commands on their computer — was the only one with no durable record. Dispatch and settlement are SEPARATE rows on purpose: a dispatch with no matching settlement is what a machine that went dark mid-task looks like, and one row written at the end would erase that. A REFUSED dispatch is recorded too, because a run of them is what an attempted bypass looks like from the outside. The other half of the suite is what must NEVER be written: EgressLedgerRow carries `path`, and the standing 18.2/FC-407 invariant is that those rows are never persisted hosted-side because a path is itself sensitive (client names live in folder names; for a legal practice a directory listing is privileged). A machine ADVERTISES what it can do in its hello frame, and selection read that list as if it were an authorisation: a pairing claiming egress.residential became a candidate to route a tenant's traffic through. Advertisement is a SELF-ASSERTION by the machine — the same category of control as J-7's model-set `confirmed`, wrong for the same reason: a daemon that is compromised, misconfigured, or simply running a newer build than its owner expected could widen its own privileges by claiming more. A capability is now usable only where the machine advertises it AND the org granted it, with DEFAULT DENY — a freshly paired machine can do nothing, which is the direction that fails safe, since inheriting whatever the machine claims makes a new machine maximally privileged exactly while nobody is watching. The router used to pick 'the newest live socket for this owner', so a step could not say which machine it needed, what that machine had to be able to do, or what should happen when the answer was none; a step written for the machine with the card reader would silently run on the laptop without one. A recipe may say WHERE the fields are and may never say what to do, because the typist is the only primitive handling a DECRYPTED credential against a LIVE page: anything steering it sits inside the credential's trust boundary. A captured session is not a token usable anywhere: it was established from a particular vantage point, and replaying one captured on a lawyer's home connection from a datacenter IP is the exact pattern fraud systems exist to flag — same cookie, different continent — with a failure mode that is an account lock or a silent shadow-ban rather than a clean error. The property this suite exists for is that WIRING GRANTS NOTHING: an ungranted capability is refused BEFORE a frame is sent (a refusal after dispatch would already have asked a user's computer to run something), a grant is re-read PER INVOCATION so a mid-run revoke stops the next step rather than the next run, and another org's grant never authorises this one.
